# Native mode: operators and edits

Generated from the operator catalog. Every operator produces one output table on out; its inputs are the tables named first in its definition.


## Edit statements

`dataflow(reasoning, actions)` exposes five actions: Inspect, Edit, Execute, Retrieve and Answer. An Edit's `changes` string contains statements, each starting at the margin:

```text
<name> = <operator>(<input>, ..., <parameter>=<value>, ...)
del <name>, ...
```

Assigning a new name creates an operator; assigning an existing name replaces its whole definition, inputs included. The input tables are the leading positional names of the call and become the operator's incoming edges in port order. Restating an operator with other inputs rewires it: each edge whose source changed is removed and the new one created; unchanged edges stay. `del` deletes operators and every incident edge, and a consumer left without an input must be restated or deleted before it executes. An operator cannot be its own input, and a name is assigned at most once per Edit. Names resolve against the graph as it stands after the whole Edit; inputs must not form a cycle. Each Edit is atomic. Execute with operator_ids runs those operators and their upstream dependencies, materializing each result. Execute without operator_ids runs the whole graph.

An Edit reports one line per change, naming a port only when the operator has several:

```text
operator totals created (aggregate)
operator orders updated (scan)
edge orders -> totals created
edge budgets -> compared.right removed
operator scratch deleted
results invalidated: orders
```

## Catalog (15 operators)

| Operator | Input ports | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `scan` | none | Read a file or glob: CSV/TSV, text, Excel, HTML, JSON or Parquet. Use format="lines", "fwf" or "whitespace" for other text layouts. preview=n reads a sample of raw lines or sheet rows; use a full scan for computation. names requires header=False; all_text=True preserves codes such as 001. sheet selects an Excel sheet or HTML table; file_column records the source. |
| `project` | in | Keep or drop columns, then rename them with {old: new}. Row order and count stay unchanged. |
| `cast` | in | Types: str, int64, float64, bool, datetime(format=..., tz=...). Write dtype names without quotes, for example amount=float64. Failed conversions raise an error, or become missing with errors="null". Naive datetimes need a timezone. |
| `filter` | in | fn(row) returns True to keep a row, False or None to drop it. Preserves order and columns. |
| `map` | in | fn(row) returns the whole new row as a dict. Use {**row, "new": value} to retain existing columns. One output row per input, with consistent keys and scalar values. |
| `aggregate` | in | One row per group; by=[] gives one row. Reducers: count(), count(col), count_distinct, sum, mean, min, max, median, stddev, first. count() counts rows; count(col) counts non-null values. Reductions skip nulls except first; an all-null sum is null. stddev is the sample standard deviation. |
| `join` | left, right | on is a column, list of columns, or [(left_col, right_col)]. how: inner, left, right, full, cross, semi, anti. semi keeps the left rows with a match, anti those without, each once, left columns only. For a cross join, omit on or use None/[]; join(how="cross") attaches a single-row benchmark to every input row. Null keys do not match by default. validate: many_to_many, one_to_one, one_to_many, many_to_one; cross uses many_to_many. A colliding right column gets suffix, repeated until free (the receipt lists renames); output order is unspecified. |
| `union` | in[0], in[1], ...; two or more | Stack tables in input order, retaining duplicates. strict requires matching schemas; align fills absent columns with null. Cast incompatible types first. |
| `distinct` | in | Keep one whole row per key (all columns by default). keep="first" or "last"; missing keys compare equal. Preserves relative row order. |
| `sort` | in | Stable sort: by=["amount"] ascending, or by=[("amount", "desc"), "name"]. nulls="first" or "last". |
| `limit` | in | Keep n rows from offset. Sort first when selecting a top-k. |
| `window` | in | Output keywords name columns: prev=lag("value") creates prev. Also lead, row_number, rank, dense_rank. Order within partitions; ranks start at 1; keep input row order. |
| `unpivot` | in | Wide to long: one output row per input row and selected column, including nulls. Remaining columns are keys; selected columns need compatible types. |
| `pivot` | in | Long to wide. Each (index, columns) pair must be unique; aggregate first if needed. Absent cells become null, null pivot keys fail. Retrieve the result to learn its new column names. |
| `process` | in[0], ..., in[n-1], one per fn parameter; none for a loader | One custom operation the catalog cannot express. fn takes one DataFrame per input, in order, and returns one DataFrame. Zero inputs are for loading unsupported formats. Keep filtering, deriving columns, joining and aggregation in predefined operators. |

## Parameters and contracts

Signatures name input tables first (`T`, `L`, `R`, `T1`, ...), then parameters with their defaults. Data types are bare names; reducers and window functions name columns.

```text
scan(files, format="auto", skip_lines=0, header=True, names=None, all_text=False, delim=None, comment=None, widths=None, sheet=None, encoding=None, file_column=None, preview=None)
    Read a file or glob: CSV/TSV, text, Excel, HTML, JSON or Parquet. Use format="lines", "fwf" or "whitespace" for other text layouts. preview=n reads a sample of raw lines or sheet rows; use a full scan for computation. names requires header=False; all_text=True preserves codes such as 001. sheet selects an Excel sheet or HTML table; file_column records the source.

project(T, keep=None, drop=None, rename=None)
    Keep or drop columns, then rename them with {old: new}. Row order and count stay unchanged.

cast(T, column=dtype, ..., errors="raise")
    Types: str, int64, float64, bool, datetime(format=..., tz=...). Write dtype names without quotes, for example amount=float64. Failed conversions raise an error, or become missing with errors="null". Naive datetimes need a timezone.

filter(T, fn, doc="what the predicate keeps")
    fn(row) returns True to keep a row, False or None to drop it. Preserves order and columns.

map(T, fn, doc="what the new row holds")
    fn(row) returns the whole new row as a dict. Use {**row, "new": value} to retain existing columns. One output row per input, with consistent keys and scalar values.

aggregate(T, by=[], name=reducer("col"), ...)
    One row per group; by=[] gives one row. Reducers: count(), count(col), count_distinct, sum, mean, min, max, median, stddev, first. count() counts rows; count(col) counts non-null values. Reductions skip nulls except first; an all-null sum is null. stddev is the sample standard deviation.

join(L, R, on=None, how="inner", nulls_equal=False, suffix="_right", validate="many_to_many")
    on is a column, list of columns, or [(left_col, right_col)]. how: inner, left, right, full, cross, semi, anti. semi keeps the left rows with a match, anti those without, each once, left columns only. For a cross join, omit on or use None/[]; join(how="cross") attaches a single-row benchmark to every input row. Null keys do not match by default. validate: many_to_many, one_to_one, one_to_many, many_to_one; cross uses many_to_many. A colliding right column gets suffix, repeated until free (the receipt lists renames); output order is unspecified.

union(T1, T2, ..., schema="strict")
    Stack tables in input order, retaining duplicates. strict requires matching schemas; align fills absent columns with null. Cast incompatible types first.

distinct(T, columns=None, keep="first")
    Keep one whole row per key (all columns by default). keep="first" or "last"; missing keys compare equal. Preserves relative row order.

sort(T, by, nulls="last")
    Stable sort: by=["amount"] ascending, or by=[("amount", "desc"), "name"]. nulls="first" or "last".

limit(T, n, offset=0)
    Keep n rows from offset. Sort first when selecting a top-k.

window(T, partition_by=[], order_by=[...], name=fn, ...)
    Output keywords name columns: prev=lag("value") creates prev. Also lead, row_number, rank, dense_rank. Order within partitions; ranks start at 1; keep input row order.

unpivot(T, columns, name="variable", value="value")
    Wide to long: one output row per input row and selected column, including nulls. Remaining columns are keys; selected columns need compatible types.

pivot(T, index, columns, values)
    Long to wide. Each (index, columns) pair must be unique; aggregate first if needed. Absent cells become null, null pivot keys fail. Retrieve the result to learn its new column names.

process(T1, ..., Tn, fn=function, doc="what it does")   or   process(fn=loader, doc="...")
    One custom operation the catalog cannot express. fn takes one DataFrame per input, in order, and returns one DataFrame. Zero inputs are for loading unsupported formats. Keep filtering, deriving columns, joining and aggregation in predefined operators.
```

## Python implementations

Keep loading, deriving columns, filtering, joining and aggregation in separate predefined operators. Use process for one operation the catalog cannot express. A custom calculation consumes its input tables; a source process loads an unsupported format and returns a parsed table for downstream operators. Build a known chain in one Edit.

Filter and map accept lambdas or functions. A filter receives a row and returns a boolean; a map receives a row and returns the complete output row. Process receives one DataFrame per input table and returns a DataFrame; its function takes one parameter per input, in order, and a zero-parameter function is a loader. Every callback operator requires doc, describing the output's meaning.

Indent complete function definitions under the operator that uses them. Helpers belong in the same block, and imports belong inside functions. Definitions do not carry across operators or updates.

```dataflow
correlation = process(measurements, fn=correlate, doc="Pearson correlation between yearly changes")
    def correlate(df):
        import pandas as pd
        return pd.DataFrame({"correlation": [df["x"].corr(df["y"])]})
```

## Execution and caching

The editor stages and validates every statement before committing. The graph's ordered input edges become the native operator's inputs, its revision and generated engine code. A changed definition or input invalidates the operator and its descendants; restating an operator unchanged invalidates nothing. Valid results on independent branches remain available. Retrieve never executes and observations preserve the result version originally returned.

Edits recorded in the earlier graph-command syntax (`create operator`, `create edge`) are rejected with a rewrite hint. Expression-mode `edits` traces remain replayable through their original interpreter.
